ops.content: The brain daemon restart protocol routes through `launchctl kickstart -k <service-target>` rather than a direct `Popen` spawn. This delegates process lifecycle management to launchd, ensuring the daemon is relaunched under the correct service context, with proper environment variables and resource limits as defined in the launchd plist. The `-k` flag kills any running instance before relaunching, making restarts idempotent and safe to call even when the daemon is in an unknown state.

ops.title: WAL checkpoint starvation under parallel sessions
ops.content: When two sessions write concurrently, the TRUNCATE checkpoint starves; symptom is an ever-growing -wal file.

connect_to.title: e5f6a7b8
connect_to.why: WAL checkpoint starvation is a direct downstream effect of SQLite writer-slot contention: concurrent sessions blocking the WAL writer prevent the TRUNCATE checkpoint from running, causing the -wal file to grow unboundedly.
